questions.q: Why is this lab's flow built as a before-save, record-triggered flow rather than after-save?
options: Before-save flows run faster for other automation on the org
After-save flows cannot use Get Records elements
The only work being done is a field update (OwnerId), which before-save flows handle without triggering a second save
Before-save is required for all flows on the Lead object
questions.explain: Setting OwnerId is a field update — before-save flows update the record in memory before the save, which is faster than an after-save flow re-saving the record.

questions.q: What does the 'Territory Match Found?' Decision element check?
options: Whether the Lead's email address is valid
Whether the flow has exceeded a governor limit
Whether the Lead was created today
Whether the Get Territory Rule query actually returned a matching Territory_Assignment__c record
questions.explain: The Decision checks whether territoryMatch is not null — i.e., whether a territory record matching the Lead's State was found.

questions.q: What happens to a Lead whose State doesn't match any Territory_Assignment__c record?
options: The flow throws an unhandled fault and the Lead save fails
The Lead is deleted automatically
The Lead's OwnerId is set to a shared Unassigned Leads queue via the Default/No Match outcome
The flow retries the query up to 10 times
questions.explain: The 'No Match' Decision outcome routes to an Assignment element that sets OwnerId to a fallback queue, ensuring the Lead is never left ownerless.

questions.q: Why does this lab's fault path write to a field instead of showing a Display Text screen like Lesson 20's example?
options: Display Text is deprecated and no longer available
Fields are always preferred over screens for error messages
The Get Records element doesn't support fault paths
Before-save and autolaunched flows can't use screen elements, so $Flow.FaultMessage is written to a field on the record instead
questions.explain: Screen elements require a screen flow; this before-save flow has no screen context, so the fault path writes the real error onto a field on the Lead record.

questions.q: Per this lab's testing step, what two scenarios should be debugged before activating the flow?
options: Only a scenario where the State matches an existing territory
A State that matches a territory, and a State that matches none — confirming both the assigned-owner and fallback-queue paths
Only a scenario that intentionally triggers the fault path
Testing is not necessary before activation
questions.explain: Both the matched and unmatched cases need to be debugged to confirm the Lead ends up with the right owner either way, before the flow goes live.
